key_insight: A flow-based generative model can learn a realistic probability distribution for turbulent channel flow, enabling synthetic turbulence generation and flow reconstruction that preserve key physical and dynamical properties.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to create physically consistent turbulent initial conditions and missing-flow reconstructions for simulation, uncertainty studies, and data-driven turbulence modeling.
method: Train a flow-based generative model on a minimal conditional flow unit in turbulent channel flow at Re_tau=180.
Introduce a consistent sampling procedure for the learned conditional distribution.
Test generated fields against DNS for ensemble statistics, conditional consistency, and dynamical invariance.
evidence_signal: Direct numerical simulation comparisons show the synthetic fields reproduce intermittency, nonlinear energy transfer, and stationary ensemble statistics when used as DNS initial conditions.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated for channel flow at Re_tau=180, so generalization to other wall-bounded flows and higher Reynolds numbers needs further validation.
paper_title: A machine-learned probability distribution in the phase space of turbulent channel flow for synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction
